issues.reason: The reviewer's own q2 gap concedes that an active object-complement small clause ('call X ADJ') is neither resultative, depictive nor finite complement -- genuine gap territory -- and the calibration line makes improvisation acceptable there: the seal emits no false or ill-typed atom, records only what the Keepers say, and correctly withholds a top-level (Member sk_plan_1 dangerous) that no other route could supply without inventing or dropping stated content.

Propositional attitudes states that 'the holder is Experiencer exactly when the complement seals' and expressly includes progressive-accepting speech verbs (announce, report, say, confirm), so once the sealing route is taken Experiencer is the rule-following choice; the objection is parasitic on issue 0 and the progressive test does not reach a sealed complement.

gaps_confirmed: active object-complement small clause with a labeling / speech verb ('call / deem / name X ADJ'): not a resultative (the calling does not make the plan dangerous), not a depictive, and not a finite clausal complement, so the stated qualifier 'dangerous' has no licensed carrier of its own
new_gaps: under the improvised seal the labeled object carries no top-level role atom on the calling event, so nothing licenses how 'what did the Keepers call dangerous?' binds the object -- an object-complement construction needs both the non-commitment and a queryable object link
notes: 'The Keepers' follows the capitalized-plural-label rule exactly (one Name-only symbol, no GroupOf, no per-member keeper typing), and the definite 'the plan' correctly projects its typing outside the seal.
